% Synthetic tables fixture — invented text, nothing from any private
% document. Exercises the booktabs default: three rule weights with their
% declared padding, p-column widths as fractions of the measure, `@{}`
% killing the outer pads, a caption below (figure convention) and above
% (table convention), `\cmidrule` with trimming, `\addlinespace`, a
% `\multicolumn` head spanning two columns, and a figure float whose
% caption binds to its body.
\documentclass{article}
\fonts{ dir = "fonts", body = "Source Serif Pro", math = "Fira Math" }

\pdfmeta{ title = "Formal Tables" }

\begin{document}

\section{Formal tables}

A table between paragraphs takes booktabs' shape: a heavier rule above and
below, a lighter one under the head, padding that belongs to the rules, and
never a vertical line.

\begin{table}
\centering
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{0.29\linewidth}p{0.55\linewidth}p{0.06\linewidth}@{}}
  \toprule
  \textbf{Construct} & \textbf{Meaning} & \textbf{Ok} \\
  \midrule
  invented row & \texttt{alpha} & yes \\
  $x \leq y$ & \texttt{beta} & yes \\
  \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{A booktabs table with \textbf{declared} spacing.}
\end{table}

\begin{table}
\caption{The caption above: the table convention.}
\centering
\begin{tabular}{lcr}
  \toprule
  & \multicolumn{2}{c}{a spanned head} \\
  left & centre & right \\
  \cmidrule(lr){1-2}
  a & b & c \\
  \addlinespace
  d & e & f \\
  \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\begin{figure}
\centering
A placeholder figure body, one centred paragraph standing in for an image.
\caption{A figure's caption, bound below what it captions.}
\end{figure}

A closing paragraph, so the last float's separation from following text is
on the page too.

\end{document}
